history.dynasty: Zamindari period (Govind Singh, zamindar of Jharsuguda); temple built 1916, renovated 1969 and recently by Paschim Odisha Bikash Parishad
history.period: Swayambhu lingam of unknown age; present temple structure from 1916 (early 20th century)
history.summary: Recognized as the original Shiva shrine ('Adyaswambhu pitha') of Jharsuguda: a self-appeared (swayambhu) Shivalingam of unknown age in a small forest just beyond Purunabasti, the old town, about 1 km from Jharsuguda railway station. During the reign of Govind Singh, zamindar of Jharsuguda, the lingam was worshipped in a thatched hut; in 1916 a Gujarati railway contractor named Mulju Jagmal erected a small temple, with the zamindar arranging sevayats and donating agricultural land for worship. The temple was renovated in 1969 by Calcutta philanthropist Surajmal Mohota and later reconstructed/enlarged by the Paschim Odisha Bikash Parishad (Western Odisha Development Council). A fair has been held here every Shivaratri since 1916. A small garden near the temple is a local picnic spot. Coordinates are Jharsuguda town-level and approximate.

name: Jhadeswar Temple
town_description: Jharsuguda is the headquarters of Jharsuguda district in western Odisha, often called the 'powerhouse of Odisha' for its coal mines and power and aluminium industries. Purunabasti (old town), just east of the railway station, is the original settlement around which the town grew. The city is a major rail junction and now has its own airport, Veer Surendra Sai Airport.
